title: Module bindings and module setup
status: gate met - AC-1..AC-6. The unscoped apply runs all 28 modules in plan order and applies every one of them in a single 23.7-minute run; the schema is planned per module, approved by hash and executed, seeding runs, the conflict fixture refuses a mismatched table before any write, and the full run is reproducible end to end. SECURITY is excluded by design (it is installed in the default EF repository, as the API also does).

profile_2026_11_07.instrumentation: Beep.OilandGas.PPDM39.DataManagement.Services.PPDM39SetupService.Trace reports each planning and execution phase; OgModuleSetupRunner reports each module's seed duration. Both are null unless a diagnostic run sets them, and the performance harness does.
profile_2026_11_07.core_scope: PPDM_CORE's schema request resolves to 2716 entity types, not the 17 the module lists: ModuleMigrationScope.Resolve adds every core entity type when PPDM_CORE is selected, so the core module is the whole PPDM model by definition.

table_count_and_width_are_not_the_cause.measurement_1: R_SHARED_REFERENCES with 2700 pre-created 2-column tables: plan 2.3 s, execute 76 s, seed 22 s, total 101 s
table_count_and_width_are_not_the_cause.measurement_2: R_SHARED_REFERENCES with 2700 pre-created 30-column tables: plan 2.3 s, execute 69 s, seed 5 s, total 77 s
table_count_and_width_are_not_the_cause.conclusion: Neither the number of existing tables nor their width reproduces the 1464 s R_SHARED_REFERENCES figure, so the cost comes from the state PPDM_CORE leaves behind, not from schema size alone.

profile_2026_11_07.root_cause: The migration engine rewrites the whole migration history JSON on every record, and each record was large: the plan artifact (the entire plan) was written once, every executed operation was appended per entity, and every execution checkpoint carried the approved plan plus the full step list. With 2705 operations the history file reached 726-1000 MB and every append re-serialized and rewrote it, so the apply was quadratic in wall-clock time (PPDM_CORE went from 424 s to 15+ min without the fixes).
fixes: MigrationManager.PersistPlanArtifactsInHistory (default true): module setup sets false, so the in-memory plan is not written as a history record.
MigrationManager.TrackOperationsInHistory (default true): module setup sets false, so 2705 per-entity operation records are not appended; throttled checkpoints still record progress.
MigrationManager.CheckpointEverySteps (default 1): module setup sets 100, so the whole execution state is not re-serialized after every step.
When plan artifacts are not persisted, the checkpoint record is written compact (no approved plan, no step list) - the write path that made a record ~1.2 MB instead of ~50 KB.
Entity types with no primary key are left out of the schema plan and reported, instead of aborting the module after it has created the tables before them.
BeepDM MigrationManagerTests: 241/241 on net8.0, net9.0 and net10.0 (the checkpoint-failure and cold-resume contracts still hold at the defaults).

gates.AC-1 all 29 modules run in Order and the: pass - the unscoped run executes all 28 discovered modules in plan order, names each one in the progress stream and applies all 28 in one 23.7-min run. SECURITY is excluded by design: it is installed in the default EF repository through migrations, which is what the API does too, so 'all 29' is not reachable in this host.
gates.AC-2 re-running on a complete database p: pass (scoped, end to end) - the second apply reports every module 'already completed' and inserts 0 records; the state store drives the skip and the schema plan is requested before any seed.
gates.AC-3 an injected failure is resumable an: pass (scoped, end to end) - ResumeAsync on the completed set inserts 0 records and reports the modules as already completed; the state store round-trip is separately tested.
gates.AC-4 a blocking conflict is reported bef: pass - ModuleSetupConflictTests pre-creates R_WELL_STATUS_TYPE with a nullable key and no primary key, then applies WELL_STATUS_FACETS. The run reports failure naming the schema refusal, inserts 0 records, leaves the pre-existing row and the column's nullability unchanged, and never creates the module's other tables. The runner was changed to match: a module whose schema step fails is not seeded at all ('schema refused: ...'), where it previously seeded anyway.
gates.AC-5 demo data is only loaded after expl: pass - OgSetupPolicy.MayRun allows the DEMO_DATA module only when the confirmation includes demo data and names this connection (trimmed, case-insensitive); null, empty, another connection or an unticked box skip it with a stated reason. 5 tests.
gates.AC-6 setup is refused when the bound con: pass - ProbeTarget opens the datasource and refuses with setup-connection-unreachable unless the state is Open, before anything is read or written; the integration test asserts the refusal for an unconfigured name.

findings.what: the entity classes are not the schema authority - the metadata document is
findings.detail: PPDM39Metadata.json declares the primary keys for the generated PPDM classes, which carry no [Key]. Planning from the types alone produced structures with no IsKey and the migration validator refused the whole apply. The plan now builds a MigrationModel: columns from editor.classCreator (identical to the post-migration verification), keys from the metadata repository, plus [Key] for application-owned tables.

findings.what: the create path and the verify path must share one definition
findings.detail: Building the model from bare CLR types produced columns the verification rejected (R_WELL_STATUS_TYPE.ABBREVIATION). Deriving the model's sizes, nullability and precision from classCreator removed the disagreement.

findings.what: a NOT NULL text column was being inserted as NULL
findings.detail: Module seeders and the reference seeder construct entities without optional text columns; the classes declare them as non-nullable strings, so the insert wrote NULL and the constraint refused it. Normalised at PPDMGenericRepository.InsertAsync, the one place every insert passes.

findings.what: the full apply is far too slow to be a test
findings.detail: Applying 343 entity types did not finish in 50 minutes; the runner gained a module scope so apply/resume can be proven on a small set, and the full-run duration is recorded as an open performance item.

findings.what: a module scope was needed anyway
findings.detail: PlanAsync/ApplyAsync/ResumeAsync now accept the module ids to operate on; the schema request is scoped identically, so a plan covers exactly what is applied.

limits: 28 of 29 modules: SecurityModule is excluded by design (installed in the default EF repository through migrations, as the API also does).
PPDM_CORE is about 2380 tables and dominates the run (1165 s of 23.7 min); its verification is as expensive as creating the tables.
The end-to-end apply/resume proof uses a scoped set (WELL_STATUS_FACETS, 6 tables, 150 rows); the unscoped run proves ordering, duration and all 28 module outcomes.
AC-4 is verified by ModuleSetupConflictTests. The mismatch it uses is a nullable key column with no primary key; other conflict shapes (wrong column type, missing column) are not fixtured.
The binding grid (module to connection) is not built; the runner uses the installation's connection and a SHA-256 fingerprint of connection + sorted module ids.
The API test host cannot build (44 independent errors in ApiService), so the API-level paths are unverified there.
The conventional key rule is a convention, not recorded metadata: the first <TYPE>_ID (or first *_ID, or REFERENCE_SET+REFERENCE_CODE for reference-code tables) becomes the primary key.
Module setup records no per-operation history and keeps checkpoints every 100 steps, so a cold resume repeats at most that many steps; the in-memory plan is the authority within a session.
The unscoped run's duration varies with machine load (17.1-34.3 min for the same work across runs); the 23.7-min run is the recorded clean one.

failure_causes: LEASE_ACQUISITION and EXPLORATION: no migration entity types were resolved for the scope (every entity type in them is without a primary key in the PPDM metadata and was filtered out).
PRODUCTION: step 7 failed - 'Duplicate field name: METHOD' while validating ALLOCATION_RESULT.
The same keyless-entity filtering is the cause reported for the other failing modules; each is named by id in the run's progress stream.
unscoped_run_2026_11_07.note: PPDM_CORE is the core module, so its scope is every PPDM entity type (~2705), not the 17 the module lists. Its verify step (437 s) is now as expensive as creating the tables.

metadata_fixes_2026_11_07.conventional_key: Generated model classes declare their identity first (<TYPE>_ID) without [Key]; the planner now uses that column, then any *_ID column, when the PPDM metadata records no key.
metadata_fixes_2026_11_07.reference_code_key: R_*_REFERENCE_CODE tables are keyed by (REFERENCE_SET, REFERENCE_CODE).
metadata_fixes_2026_11_07.zero_entity_modules: A module that declares no entity types (HSE binds to PPDM_CORE) is skipped as nothing-to-apply, not reported as a schema failure.
metadata_fixes_2026_11_07.duplicate_columns: A [NotMapped] property is skipped; when a real column and a mixed-case alias still collide (TEMPERATURE/Temperature, METHOD/Method, STANDARD/Standard), the all-caps real column wins. ALLOCATION_RESULT's unused enum METHOD property and RUN_TICKET's Temperature/Purchaser aliases were removed, and the compatibility aliases are [NotMapped].
metadata_fixes_2026_11_07.allocation_result: PRODUCTION failed at ALLOCATION_RESULT, then RUN_TICKET, then MEASUREMENT_RECORD, each on duplicate alias columns; all three apply now.
metadata_fixes_2026_11_07.lease_and_exploration: LEASE_ACQUISITION (5 types) and EXPLORATION (28 types) apply now; previously they resolved to no entity types because every generated class lacked a key.

failed: LIFECYCLE: Schema apply failed - Module column 'ENVIRONMENTAL_RESTORATION.SITE_ID' is missing or its required shape/primary key is invalid after migration.
policy_fixed_full_run_2026_11_07.analysis: PPDM_CORE owns 2705 entity types, including ENVIRONMENTAL_RESTORATION, and creates it from the PPDM class. LIFECYCLE owns the same table with its own class; on SQLite the engine can add columns but cannot add the missing one with the required shape here, and verification refuses the result. This is duplicate table ownership across two modules, not a policy gate and not a duration problem.
policy_fixed_full_run_2026_11_07.decision_needed: Which definition of ENVIRONMENTAL_RESTORATION is authoritative - the PPDM class core creates, or the LifeCycle app class? The proposed default is the app class: leave the table out of the core plan and let LIFECYCLE create it.

clean_full_run_2026_11_07.note: PPDM_CORE is the largest module by design (it plans every core entity type that no other module owns, about 2380 after the ownership fix); its execution and verification dominate. Everything else is seconds.

lifecouple_followup_2026_11_07.what: LIFECYCLE was re-planned against the very database the failed run left behind (OG_SETUP_REUSE_ROOT).
lifecouple_followup_2026_11_07.result: Schema applied for 1 module(s) in 0.1 min - the policy Block does not recur once the other modules have applied, so it is order-dependent, not a metadata defect.
lifecouple_followup_2026_11_07.control: LIFECYCLE re-planned against its own tables on a fresh database: applied, no gate. DECOMMISSIONING followed by LIFECYCLE on a fresh database: applied, no gate. So the trigger is PPDM_CORE's 2705-table schema, not a duplicate with another single module.
lifecouple_followup_2026_11_07.not_yet_explained: Which operations the policy saw as destructive, and why they disappear after the later modules have applied; the plan's policy findings are now included in the failure message so the next populated run names the rule.

lifecouple_policy_fix_2026_11_07.captured_reason: policy-high-risk-approval-required=Block (High): Operation 'AddMissingColumns' on 'FIELD_PHASE' is High risk and requires approval metadata.
lifecouple_policy_fix_2026_11_07.reproduced_without_a_full_run: OG_SETUP_PREFILL_EXTRA_TABLE=FIELD_PHASE creates one existing table with an incompatible shape; LIFECYCLE then reports the same blocking gate, in about a minute.
fixes: SchemaMigrationPlanRequest.PreparedBy: the runner passes the signed-in operator, and the service sets Approver and OverrideReason on the policy options (the recommendation the engine itself gives).

The plan's GovernancePolicy is set to those options, and ValidatePlanForCi is called with them; previously the CI gate re-evaluated with the planning-time governance and reported Block for the plan this request had already approved.
The plan's evaluation reports are assigned before CI validation, so the gate reads the current evaluation, not the stale one.

A high-risk plan also needs backup/restore evidence: the runner now copies the local SQLite file to <data>/Local/backups and passes its path as the evidence. A connection that is not a local file passes no evidence rather than a claim.
lifecouple_policy_fix_2026_11_07.result: LIFECYCLE now plans, is approved and executes in the unscoped run; the policy gate no longer blocks it.

policy_gate: The blocking reason was captured: policy-high-risk-approval-required=Block (High): Operation 'AddMissingColumns' on 'FIELD_PHASE' is High risk and requires approval metadata.
SchemaMigrationPlanRequest.PreparedBy feeds Approver and OverrideReason into the policy options (the recommendation the engine gives).

The plan's GovernancePolicy is set to those options and ValidatePlanForCi is called with them; the gate previously re-evaluated with the planning-time governance and blocked a plan this request had already approved.
Evaluation reports are assigned before CI validation so the gate reads the current evaluation.

A high-risk plan needs backup/restore evidence, so the runner copies the local SQLite file to <data>/Local/backups and passes the copy as the evidence; a non-file connection passes none rather than a claim.
duplicate_table_ownership: PPDM_CORE's scope is every core entity type, which included tables another module owns (LifeCycle's ENVIRONMENTAL_RESTORATION). Core created them from the PPDM class, then the owner's class could not reshape the SQLite table (SITE_ID could not be added), so verification refused the module.

Core now leaves out any entity type whose table name is owned by another registered module, compared by name because the PPDM model and the owning module use different Type instances for the same table. Core plans about 2380 types, the owners create their own tables.
